summary:
We developed STAR FALL, a 2D pixel-art educational adventure combining space mission design, resource management, and environmental learning. Players follow astronaut Nick and robot companion Bill after a space-time rift strands Nick on a polluted future Earth.

Players first construct the spacecraft VELA, choosing components and balancing budget, mass, fuel, and electrical resources. After the crash, they recover essential technology, rebuild the ship, and evaluate return-flight configurations through simplified mission simulations. Interactive encounters teach waste identification and sorting, while a typing-based boss battle introduces environmental vocabulary with English definitions.

STAR FALL addresses the challenge by connecting mission objectives, engineering choices, limited resources, and simulation feedback within a continuous adventure. Players experience how individual decisions affect the success of an entire mission.

The project makes technical concepts approachable for younger learners while encouraging environmental responsibility. Its central message is simple: exploring space should deepen our commitment to protecting the home we already have.
details:
STAR FALL is a single-player educational adventure that combines space mission design, environmental learning, and English vocabulary practice through 2.5D pixel-art gameplay. Designed for children and students, it turns technical and environmental concepts into interactive challenges within a continuous story.

Players follow Nick, a human astronaut, and Bill, his robot companion. The journey begins on present-day Earth, where players construct the spacecraft VELA, select equipment, manage a budget, and complete preflight checks. A fictional space-time rift then strands Nick on an imagined, polluted future Earth. To return home, players explore abandoned facilities, recover essential technology, and reconstruct their spacecraft.

The game includes three distinct educational encounters. In the waste-sorting arena, players identify materials and switch between STAR FALL’s Green, Blue, and Yellow categories to defeat waste-armored enemies. They then clean and collect dropped energy cores to power a recovery station. A short illustrated guide introduces the rules, while layered materials and contaminated containers encourage players to consider an item’s condition rather than relying only on its shape.

The second encounter uses directional shield defense. Players block hostile energy, allow beneficial energy through, and decide when to spend accumulated charge on a counterattack. The final encounter introduces environmental vocabulary through a typing battle. Each correctly entered letter fires a projectile, while English definitions help connect spelling with meaning. Vocabulary progresses from basic to more advanced terms.

Spacecraft construction and reconstruction directly address the mission-design challenge. Players balance mass, propellant, electrical power, stored energy, payload, and route requirements. A simplified simulator explains why a configuration succeeds or fails, allowing players to revise their choices. We used NASA Goddard’s Mission Design Lab as an engineering reference for connecting mission requirements, alternative designs, trade-offs, and resource budgets. The game’s numerical specifications remain simplified gameplay values. Resource: Mission Design Lab.

We developed STAR FALL using Godot 4 and statically typed GDScript, with JSON for gameplay configuration and educational content. Python utilities support generated audio, while Visual Studio Code and Git support development and version control. Claude and Codex assisted with planning, implementation support, and documentation. The game targets standard desktop or laptop computers using a keyboard and mouse, without specialized hardware or a continuous internet connection.

Our team considered readable graphics, consistent controls, gradual difficulty, concise explanations, checkpoint recovery, and the balance between entertainment and learning. The project’s creative contribution is connecting engineering decisions, material identification, reflex-based defense, vocabulary practice, and environmental storytelling within one adventure.

Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity, experimentation, and environmental responsibility. Rather than presenting protection of Earth as a final slogan alone, STAR FALL makes observation, careful resource use, and informed decisions part of how players progress.
